newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares lose 1.64 pct in continued selling.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares lose 1.64 pct in continued selling.

text.p: Istanbul shares continued their downward technical move on Friday, falling below the 90,000 mark in search of fresh support, brokers said.
The IMKB-100 closed 1,486.64 points, or 1.64 percent lower at 89,336.86, bringing weekly losses to 5.37 percent from last Friday's all-time high close of 94,407.22.
It had leapt 2.89 percent last week and 5.49 percent the previous week and hit nine record closes in the last two weeks.
Trade volume shrank to 14.47 trillon lira ($138.7 million) from Thursday's 17.01 trillion ($163.3 million).

"Prices have neared bottom. There was no activity other than a few shares. The market preferred to wait rather than buy because any negative news can produce a sharp fall," said Guray Gunay from Demirbank.
Rumours that Standard & Poor's might downgrade Turkey's credit rating soon, after putting it under Creditwatch in July triggered selling on Wednesday.
Cancellation by the constitutional court of a law allowing the government to sell state property also sparked heavy selling on Thursday.
"The index may drift sideways between 88,500 support and 91,000 until the New Year," Gunay said.
